==English==

===Etymology===
From {{m|en|put up}} + {{m|en|with}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{audio|en|En-au-put up with.ogg|a=AU}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|<,,put>}}

# {{lb|en|idiomatic|informal}} To {{l|en|endure}}, {{l|en|tolerate}}, {{l|en|suffer}} through, or allow, especially something {{l|en|annoying}}.
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:tolerate}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''put up with''' a lot of nonsense, but this is too much.}}
#* {{quote-av|en|title={{w|Before Midnight (2013 film)|Before Midnight}}|year=2013|medium=motion picture|role=Celine|actor=w:Julie Delpy|writer=w:Richard Linklater; w:Julie Delpy; w:Ethan Hawke|passage=Will you be able to '''put up with''' me for another 56 more years?}}
# To be taken in; to be sheltered (''[[put up]]'').
